items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you play with Watrous and Rosolino (unintelligible) this year at Dick Gibson's? [INTERVIEWEE] Not this year. Last year I did. Al Grey played with them this year. But last year I played with them.

ctx.x: Who else was there this year? I didn't see the Lineup (inaudible)...

Well, the trombones was -- were Watrous, Rosolino, Carl Fontana, Vic Dickinson, myself, Al Grey, George Masso. And the trumpets were -- trumpets were Clark Terry, and Ruby Braff, Pee Wee Erwin, Joe Wilder, and Jon

items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999

ctx.x: Oh yeah. We didn’t really talk about maybe just a few of your influences, on the trombone, besides your father. You mentioned a couple of influences, Lou McGarrity or did you sub for him?

I subbed for Cutty Cutshall, that’s who I subbed for, but I knew Lou and Lou was a wonderful trombone player. Vic Dickinson was one of my favs at that time, and Trummy Young I loved. Of course Urbie Green and J.J., to say nothing of Frankie Rosolino and Carl, Carl Fontana frankly for me is my all together hands down favorite of them all. I don’t think there’s anyone today on the scene that is a match for Carl Fontana. He is incredible. Absolutely. Great trombone player. © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
Okay, so I don’t usually ask this question, but if you tried to be real honest about where you fit in the list of trombone players—
